tips.comment: The penny seems to be dropping with Media Mogul having won his last two in first time cheekpieces. The 2nd and 4th from his win at Wolverhampton last time have both won since and a 3lbs rise doesn't look enough to halt further progress from a mark of 71 with the yard in good form (25% last 14 days).
6-year-old who is now 2 lb below last winning mark and should be fit to run well after a recent run last month after a break. Won three times last year and can win more having ideal race conditions.
Feel like Jagetime offers a lot of upside here, and the father-son combo of the Loughnanes tends to bear quite a lot of fruit.

My vote here goes to Off The Bench who's turn to strike is near in very good time was last seen at Bath 15 day's ago where finishing a never nearer 4th/8 now he did shape with plenty of promise and he really is starting to get the hang of things however the drop in trip to 5 furlongs on that occasion wasn't ideal and 6 furlongs looks to be the best option distance wise and that is the distance he will be racing over here today and is likely to be shown in much better light here over a more suitable trip is now lurking on an extremely dangerous mark of 56 and this gelded son of Ardad & Davinci Dawn ( Dam's sire Poet's Voice ) looks poised to strike of this sort of mark especially having found a suitable looking race to fit into here jockey Finley Marsh takes the ride on J S Moore's inmate and he must enter calculations in a race of this nature
If tuned up and ready to go, this horse's relation to Subastar suggests that they will easily get the trip and can win first time.

Stable in form, and this has winning experience at this track and is well drawn for the hat-trick. With the jockey claiming 3 lbs, same mark as when winning LTO at Nottingham on quick ground. Shapes like an improved performer this season.

I honestly wasn't expecting to get an e/w price for this one in this 9-runner race when I went through the form, and 8/1 rates excellent value with one of the very best jockeys booked in this apprentice race. This horse has a great record at the course and was sent off 3/1f in a similar race here last time out when beaten 2 lengths. Crucially though, that jockey has yet to ride a winner (she's only had 2 places in her short career too), and I suspect the switch on jockey here could hold the key. That run last time out was the horse's seasonal debut, and he usually comes on for a run, so everything looks set for a big run. Ideally, he'd prefer the ground a little less quick, but at the prices, I think he's worth siding with.
Safari Dream is far from convincing, but in this field, I think the horse has a pretty good chance against these peers

Only outing here was last year in a Class 5 race, ending with a place, 3 of 11 in a Class 5 race. Drops down here to a lower grade and runs off 3lb lower than the last outing here. Stable is also in very good form.
Palmeira's Dam has an interesting pedigree and is well-related. If taking on some of that ability, it will be able to go close here.

Had a nibble at the 3/1 around yesterday, and arguments can be made he's now too short. However, he is match fit. Form beating The Foxes is looking stronger now, and with 10.5 million in prize money, he is obviously a classy horse. Hasn't actually run over further than 1m4f so far, but he keeps on well over that trip, and the Good to Firm can only be a positive for his chances of staying the trip. Appleby is running to a 42% strike currently, and with doubts over others' fitness, he is the bet here. Sweet William will be one for the rest of the season; however, he will likely need this run and is on the shorter side for him anyway.

Epic Poet seems a little overpriced here despite the tactical race scenario likely not suiting. This horse finished a close second behind Byzantine Dream, who went on to run a cracker in a Japanese Group 1. He finished third next time when not far behind Double Major, which is a Group 1 horse. Rebel's Romance could probably get away with the 2 miles here, as I'm expecting a very weak pace. At the prices, I think this is the correct play.

See The Fire ran well enough on reappearance for me to take her here. Her two best runs last year were on good to firm ground and one of those was at this course. In my opinion she could develop into a Group 1 winning filly this season, like Bluestocking did after winning this race.

The 4yo filly spent last year running to a decent level overseas in good races. Decent UK run on her return at the start of this month when 3rd in a Group 2 race, up against Group 1 capable runners. Can improve for the run in this Group 2 contest. William Buick in the saddle and no problem with the quick ground.
Looks sure to run a big race. He looks the EW steal, but I just feel See The Fire is a bit better. She is regally bred.

ROYAL DRESS looks worth chancing at 16/1 each way in this 8-runner affair as she has won her last two seasonal debuts. She is also stepping up in trip to 1m2f for the first-time and she shaped when winning a Group 3 race at the Curragh last July like the extra distance would suit. For a more detailed write-up please see my X feed.
Interesting to see this horse come over from Italy for a tilt at British races this season. Hasn't done much wrong to be honest and happy to back at a big each way price here.

I’m backing Ambiente Amigo in the 15:13 at York ??' she’s coming into this off the back of a smart win at Nottingham, and looks like she’s still improving. That was her first try at 1m6f, and she saw it out really well, suggesting she’s got the stamina for a strong-run race like this.
She’s now dropping slightly in trip to 1m5½f, which could actually suit even better ??' especially at a track like York where things can get tactical. She’s clearly in good form and moving the right way.
Harry Davies keeps the ride after guiding her to victory last time, and that continuity is a big plus. He gave her a confident ride and knows how to get the best out of her.
This is a step up in class, but she’s unexposed compared to most of the field and still open to plenty of improvement. If she builds on that Nottingham run, she’s got a serious chance here.
At the odds, Ambiente Amigo looks like a value each-way play in a competitive race.

Race fitness would probably be the main concern here. However, it was a nice horse last season, winning 4 out of 7 and ran a nice race, finishing 6th in the Breeders' Cup Juvenile despite dwelling at the start and running keen throughout before being short of room in the last furlong. Form ties in closely with Big Mojo, who's since come out and won and is undoubtedly the best horse in this if turning up.

Tropical Storm finished 4th behind Aesterius in a Group 2 at Doncaster in September but had previously run well when winning a Listed race here at York on good to firm. In receipt of five pounds from the favourite, he might turn the tables.
Take Star Of Mehmas at the prices. I feel he has got plenty of upside in this field, and with Ryan Moore riding his usual consistent style, he has to go close.

Sir Yoshi ran a very credible 3rd at this course and distance last season, and could be suited by a forecasted fast pace once again. He's run his best races on fast ground, which he will be getting here once again.

Harry's Girl had an amazing debut. There was a moment in which she was searching for room, but when she found it, she showed some amazing speed. I thought she didn't even like the track and that a flat track like York will be much more to her liking. Richard Hannon is in great form.

Thunder Run ended last season with a very promising run at Ascot, and he'll surely build on that this season. He was quite poor on reappearance as he got tired quite quickly. I'm not sure why they decided to step him up in distance, but this horse could be out of handicaps sooner rather than later.

Salanca's win on the AW last time out was clearly something of a surprise when he beat genuine 100 rated horses. He races here off 98 and even the short head 2nd to Endless Victory last year in a hot race at HQ has plenty of clues that he's more than capable of winning this. Clearly that win last time out shows that this 4yo is still improving and there's so much superb collateral form that he simply can't be ignored at a generous looking 6/1.

Drawn with the pace but unlikely to be too close and should be able to sit off. Winner and placed at this level, including win off 94 and 0.5L 3rd off 99. Decent season last season despite only winning one, had plenty of good runs in decent handicaps. Two good runs this season when keeping on well for 2nd over 1m and being beat 0.5L 2nd at Chester from stall 12, having sweated up and raced wide. Should be hitting peak fitness now and Easterby going to 18% SR. Plenty of pace from Thunder Run, Salamanca, and a couple others, and unlikely they'll be able to sustain it here over a CD where the bias heavily favors horses mid-held up. Also has strength advantage over the 4yos as they won't have matured fully until around August.

Zain Blue has saved his best for York, finishing 2nd behind Battle Cry in his maiden (that rival a Group 3 winner since), then 5th and 1st in two handicaps over C&D, winning from a mark of 83 in first-time cheekpieces. Headgear left off for his reappearance but now goes back on and he's just 2 lbs higher than his win here in September. Up in grade but looks fairly weighted and well drawn (stall 8) with Thunder Run going forward from stall 4. Yard are in decent form having had a few winners in the last couple of weeks.
Tadej was staying on at Ascot after getting outpaced behind Wise Approach but was not beaten far in 4th place and should turn the tables in receipt of five pounds over an extra furlong at York.
Merchant was staying on over ten furlongs at Newmarket first time out this season. He should be suited by the extra distance and fast going at York and is two pounds well in with the handicapper.

The model I run suggests Many Men can win this one. This result has largely been driven by Many Men having the second highest RPR of the field, but the second lowest OR. This leaves him carrying the second lowest weight over this 1m 3f trip. Jack Doughty on board claims a further 3 lbs, which is helpful. Stall 6 draw isn't the best, but very manageable over the longer distance.

Top weight to the fore in this in recent renewals, so Anniversary must be respected on that trend alone. But I’m taking a chance on Novelista, who will have to prove he can take to the surface. That said, he’s related to a couple that acted on quick ground, as did his dam, so I see no reason why he won’t. His dam won over this trip and further, so the step up in trip should be fine, and he looks as well handicapped as anything in here off 75, which gives him a featherweight carry too. Having won 4 of the last 9 renewals, Mark Johnstone knows the toe for the race, so hopefully he’s had some say over this horse coming here.
Stumps or Slips won in a hack canter at Ffos Las last time out. Carries a 7 lbs penalty for that win, but won with plenty in hand and can win again before the handicapper catches up with him.

The model I run suggests the value play here is Leitrim Chief each way. The market leader for this race is incredibly short-priced currently. This model simulation result has been driven by Leitrim Chief having the joint highest RPR of the field, but a significantly lower official ranking compared to the market leader Stumps Or Slips. Leitrim Chief therefore goes out carrying 12 lbs less over this 2m 4f trip. Last run 69 days ago when being pulled, so race fitness might be the main concern here.
Given far too much to do last time out, and although novicey over the hurdles, absolutely flew home to nearly win. Should win here.

The model I run suggests Cuban Cigar could cause an upset here and is the value play. Cuban Cigar lines up in this 7-horse race with by far the highest RPR, but the lowest OR. This subsequently leaves him carrying the lowest weight of the 7 runners. He is a previous distance winner over this 2m trip and has Alan Doyle on board claiming a further 5 lbs off his back.

I like the chances of Kinbara Firstdraft here at Perth. He is used to travelling over 4f further than this 2m so the distance shouldn't be an issue. I like his last two runs at Down Royal & Ayr, especially the Ayr run. He was travelling very nicely into the race before hitting 2 and seemed to knock him. So if he jumps well and gets a clear round, I'm expecting him to go close. 3 places on offer with bet365 and others.

The model I run suggests Gonnino can win this one. This result has been driven by Gonnino lining up with the second highest PRR of the group. All 11 runners line up carrying the same weight. Last ran 38 days ago, so racing fitness shouldn't be an issue. Gary Rutherford has a high RTF%.

The horse won on its only other previous visit to the course in September 2024 in Class 4 on good, off a mark of 114. It also won on the last run over today's 24f trip at Ffos Las in Class 4 on good to soft, off a mark of 116. That win came 28 days ago, and the horse is upped a further 5lb. Team Bowen won this race last year with the top weight and aren't making the 854-mile round trip for a day out.

Blundered away any chance last time when sixth at Haydock. Back at this track that suits, can get back on track and get another win. Looks in form having been runner-up before last start, and although hasn't won for two years, is 18lb below last winning mark now.

The model I run suggests Everyday Champagne is the value bet here. Everyday Champagne lines up with the second highest RPR of the runners but has the lowest official ranking. This leaves him carrying the lowest weight in the race by some distance. The next lowest weight being carried is 10 lbs more, and the market leading horse is carrying the heaviest amount, it's a weight differential of 21 lbs, which is significant over what is essentially a 3m round trip.

The model I run suggests Borders Eagle to win is the value play here. This result has largely been driven by Borders Eagle having the second highest RPR of the field. The market here seems to be favoring the runners carrying the lowest weight, but the weight differential to the higher-rated horses is quite small for a 2m trip.
Take Go Go Chicago to run a big race here. Came second to confirm some semblance of ability last time out and looked a worthy adversary. Unconvinced by the favorite and happy to side with this horse.

The model I run suggests Each Way on Belle Of Annandale is the value play here. Hay Meadow is the short-priced favorite but does go out carrying over 23 lbs more. Belle Of Annandale is racing for only the second time since a previous wind operation and looks to get over the line first in what looks like a very reasonable mark.

Not sure the odds will get any better with Thankyouandplease for this Class 5 handicap hurdle tomorrow so I'm taking them now. Pulled out today at Newton Abbot. A very comfortable 3rd place at Newton Abbot last time out, I'm sure he could of gone better than that as he looked like he had more in the tank when he was finishing. Could be hard to beat.

The model I run suggests Sambezi should win this race. This model result has been driven by Sambezi having by far the highest RPR of the field and a kind official ranking. This leaves him carrying only effectively the second lowest weight of the 8-runner field. Sambezi is a previous course and distance winner, last ran 25 days ago, meaning race fitness shouldn't be an issue. Also has the highest top speed by quite a margin.

The model I run suggests an upset here for Ultra Viers. This simulated result has largely been driven by Ultra Viers having the highest RPR of the field, and a fairly low official ranking compared to the other 7 runners. This leaves him running on a very workable mark and goes out carrying 1 stone and a half less than the current market favourite. Last ran 20 days ago. Needs to show some improvement after going 4,4,4 but open to doing that off this mark.

The model I run has simulated this race and suggests Rockola should win this one. Rockola lines up with the second highest RPR of the field but has the lowest official ranking of the 7 runners. This leaves him carrying the lowest weight of the runners over this 2m 5f round trip.
Seemingly held in high regard throughout his career, Danton has been very disappointing of late. This is a guess here, but a very good chance if running to ability.

the model I run suggests Hatos could cause a bit of an upset here. Others more prominent in the early market but this looks like the value play. Hatos has by far the highest RPR of the 5 runners here. Does go out carrying a stone more than the others over the 2m race. Joe Tizard has a high RTF %. Didn't look too out of place when last running in a class 2 handicap 48 days ago, now drops back to a class 5 handicap chase and could cause an upset.

CD winner. Had its first run here on 25th April, after a 10-month layoff. Finished a respectable 4th from 10 runners, not far away. Returns here at its favored distance and going. Also likes a small field, as it idles at the rear on the majority of runs, keeping up with the pace of the front runners. 1st and 2nd favorites each carry 7lb penalties, with average time on the clock when finishing. Romanor has a 3-second faster time win, including a class 2 event. Trainer clearly feels this horse is ready for a big run.

The model I run suggests Hard Stare can win this one. This model result has been driven by Hard Stare having by far the highest RPR of the lineup. No official ranking data to go by, but all horses are carrying weights within a fairly tight banding. None of the jockeys on board are claiming, so this represents a true picture of the weight distribution. Hard Stare wears a tongue tie for the first time to aid concentration.

The model I run suggests 'She Is For Me Boys' should win this one. Lines up with by far the highest RPR of the field and steps out carrying similar weight to most of the other horses running. Top of the market, 'The Secret Pearl' carries an extra 7 lbs and could be telling over the 2m 1f trip.

This horse's only race here was his 2nd race when staying on powerfully into third over 3 furlongs less. That was in a novice race where the winner has since won off 92, the 2nd off 94, and the 4th and 5th have won decent races too. Clearly, with this extra trip certain to suit, and a very good apprentice booked, this mark of 84 is clearly a winnable one. It would be no surprise to see the 9/4 get snapped up since he looks more like a 6/4 shot to me.

Makes handicap debut on a fair-looking mark and could have been well placed here from a trainer who has a 25% win rate at this track in the last five years. This 3-year-old showed potential in three starts last year, all at 6f, and the extra furlong now tried looks likely to suit.

Decent consistent form since returning from a break in January with a win at Southwell, two 2nds and a recent 3rd at Nottingham. Has a decent low draw here and the added tongue tie might improve performance further.

This horse has a record of a win and a second in 2 races over C&D, the win being by an eased down 5 lengths. She's 6lb higher in the handicap now, but I like the jockey switch, and she clearly acts well around here, so could well be up to defying this higher mark. The trainer has won with 2 of her last 5 runners, and she's a well-bred horse for this level of racing.
Comes out of a high-class race that will prove to be better than the grade, in my opinion. At these odds and with the places, I think this represents great odds.

A wide-open handicap where Beltadaay appeals at a big-looking 14/1. He ran well for a long way on his seasonal reappearance at Beverley last month and will be fitter for that. He won well on his final start last season, and if he can get his own way up front here, he may be difficult to pass.

This is a competitive low-grade 3YO handicap on a polytrack, where several are unexposed or switching surfaces, but one stands out here. Moostar has won a maiden before and is a lightly raced horse with a slight class edge over many. Shaped okay when midfield at Windsor in a bigger field, and he drops back into what looks an easier race on a polytrack debut. He could take a step forward here and is dangerous to ignore, in my opinion.

Lightly raced handicapper who shapes like this trip will bring more improvement after a battling 2nd at Southwell on the comeback over 7f when strong at the finish. Stable does well with these sorts of types.

Won last year under today's rider and should be race-fit after a recent start back from the winter break. Should go well, running to last season's best form. Stable is getting winners, and they try cheekpieces that could add to the chance.
Related to Caernafon and given as much chance as any of them here based on pedigree. I think the odds are far too big and worth an each-way bet.

Has a high draw to contend with, but was pipped by a head here last time out less than two weeks ago and goes off at a similar mark. There are question marks on a lot of the others including a long break for the favourite who has bottom draw.
Did well last season, placed from a pound higher on her final start. Well below that level on her 2023 return, but she is entitled to improve for the effort, and this is a drop in grade for her.
Was very disappointing at Yarmouth last time, but I'm happy to take the chance that this horse can do it, with 4 places available.

SEARCHINGTHEBLUES showed plenty of ability last year on the AW, especially around a bend. Was given a quiet ride at Newmarket last time, which will put her spot on here on a return back to favorable conditions. Small bet at the prices. Should outrun her odds.

Cafe Con Leche is fairly useful on his day and a previous course winner. Didn't run badly at a higher level 3 days ago and has a big class drop here into claiming company and has solid form to boot. With a 3-pound claimer onboard, he is the one to beat if handling the quick turnaround.
A point winner and placed 2nd in a bumper before joining Henry De Bromhead. Much improved run latest when 3rd in a maiden hurdle. Normal improvement should put him in the mix.

Sets the standard on ratings and has gone close a couple of times. Could now get first win in a race lacking depth. Ran sixth last time at the Punchestown Festival, and this is a big drop back in class.
Irina's Path has very modest form but ran respectably when 4th at Sligo two days ago. Definitely fit and relatively consistent. We could get a place here at a higher odds price than the faves.

Big Dispute got an excellent 2nd just 3 days ago at Killarney and he looks well treated by the handicapper based on that run and is clearly in form. If he gets going today, he's a major player here and the odds on it will drop.
Not shown much yet, but on better ground can improve. From a top in-form stable, the addition of cheekpieces for the first time could be the answer.

Top rated and looks to have conditions to suit. Must have strong claims of winning in a poor-looking race. Best of three starts came at Naas with a very close third-place finish, and a repeat should be good enough.

This mares’ novice hurdle doesn’t look overly strong, and several are unexposed. Moonlit Mist is a useful flat winner and now makes a hurdles debut. The trainer, David H Kelly, has had success with similar types of horses and should be taken seriously here in a weak race. If the flat ability holds, she could be very dangerous if her jumping holds up.

6-year-old who gets ideal race conditions here and, on best form, should beat this field. Won on the flat twice and has also won over hurdles that came over this course and distance and reverts back to a hurdle here.

This looks like a modest and open handicap hurdle, and my selection is Mountain Port. Tailed off at Punchestown on stable debut, but previous form was better and has won a maiden hurdle. With some improvement and now settled in, if stepping up here with past ability, definitely not ruled out at 33/1 today.

Carsons Dreamboat was a very poor 8th in one hurdle run 16 months ago. Seems bad, but after a long layoff and switching into a bumper race now, it comes from a good trainer and yard, Gordon Elliott. This helps the case and will be a dark horse if fitness is raring to go. EW shout.

Answering switches back to hurdles today after a fall over the bigger fences, and this will be safer, safer, and it suits him better. His form has been, let's say, 'variable,' but he is very capable of sneaking into the frame on his best day, and the odds are big enough for the EW play here.
